reports.title: Individuality Precedes Coherent Form
reports.dek: Each Flow Lenia run begins as a seeded, continuous multichannel field that is still reorganizing, and although our first experiments asked whether a disturbed run would recover the organization and trajectory of its matched undisturbed counterpart, the clearer pattern was already visible in the different futures opened by nearby interventions.
reports.question: When does a seeded field begin to behave as an individual whose history changes both its reachable futures and the meaning of an intervention?
reports.answer: In the prospective cohort, nearby futures reorganized before a persistent body was obvious; across separate experiments, responses became more history-specific and the system grew harder to rewrite, even though its descendants did not converge on one final shape.
reports.next_question: Can the early response address predict how a completely new genotype will react, and can an intervention change that address as well as the visible body?

reports.title: Flow Lenia Causal Emergence: A Guide
reports.dek: This short entrance begins with the seeded field and introduces the campaign through the concrete changes we measured: histories become easier to distinguish, the same push loses leverage with age, and later bodies remain different even when they briefly look alike.
reports.question: What have we been doing in Flow Lenia, and what does it mean here to say that an organism appears before its silhouette?
reports.answer: Before a coherent body is easy to see, the system already carries a structured map from interventions to futures; as development continues, that map becomes more history-specific and more resistant to rewriting.
reports.next_question: The main synthesis follows these measurements across the full study, while the featured reports show where each claim was tested directly.

reports.title: Whole-Field Organization Rises Before Coherent Form
reports.dek: A whole-over-parts predictive measurement rose before an independently defined seed transition, so the field became more informative as a coordinated whole before it sustained a visibly non-square body.
reports.question: Does coordination across the whole field change before a seeded Flow Lenia run becomes visibly organism-like?
reports.answer: In a prospective cohort, the pre-transition rise was positive in fifteen of sixteen family means, which makes this a reproducible temporal signal rather than a single attractive specimen.
reports.next_question: Does the same early coordinate forecast how tightly the state constrains later transitions, and can a direct intervention move that constraint?

reports.title: Different Early Histories Produce Different Responses by Passage Eight
reports.dek: Eight passages after the field was seeded, four states made by different early pulse histories still looked similar. After the same later interventions, however, the mean distance among their passage-900 outcomes was about 4.3 times the mean distance among their shapes at passage eight. By passage 32, those histories were easier to see in the present form, while the spread in later formation times had narrowed.
reports.question: When do different early histories begin to change what the same later intervention can do: only after the body is visible, or already at the first checkpoint we measured?
reports.answer: Already by passage eight, the four nearly matched shapes responded differently to the shared challenge panel. Because passages eight through 32 reuse the same organisms, the age curve describes how one cohort changed rather than four independent replications.
reports.next_question: Which part of that early breadth comes from spatial organization, and which part is generic sensitivity to being disturbed?

reports.title: Spatial Organization Constrains Later Futures
reports.dek: Exact block rearrangements preserved genotype, channel masses, occupied material, and almost the entire outside field, while changing how clearly nearby actions separated and how explosively distant futures spread.
reports.question: If different interventions already produce different futures at passage eight, what does the field's spatial organization contribute to development?
reports.answer: Organization made local actions more legible and development faster and more reliable, while scrambling opened a broader but less disciplined collection of later futures.
reports.next_question: Can the lost constraint be rebuilt continuously, and does development reach an age at which the original repair no longer belongs to the state?

reports.title: Transition Timing Narrows Before Coherent Form
reports.dek: The same eight inventory-preserving pushes produced a broad range of transition times in some pre-form states and a narrow range in others, even though their microscopic field outcomes remained diverse.
reports.question: Before a visible transition, has the state already committed to when that transition will occur?
reports.answer: Higher whole-over-parts organization predicted a narrower range of transition times across new states, while the microscopic outcomes still remained diverse.
reports.next_question: Can an early push move a sibling state toward that committed regime and reduce the futures still available to it?

reports.title: Intervention Rankings Shift Before Formation
reports.dek: A fresh cohort reproduced the rotation of the information-response landscape before visible formation, while the intervention that maximized the score did not act as a universal lever on transition timing.
reports.question: Does the change in the information score merely mark this developmental stage, or does it also drive the later body transition?
reports.answer: The score changed again, but interventions toward higher and lower values changed sign and remained organism-specific. The score therefore marked the stage without providing a universal way to control it.
reports.next_question: Which state-dependent interventions can follow this changing response well enough to control later development?

reports.title: State-Aware Control Preserves a Wider Range of Responses
reports.dek: A controller that tested five pulse sizes at each passage usually chose one strong early intervention and then restraint, and the resulting difference between alternative causal histories persisted for eight passages after control ended.
reports.question: Can feedback hold a developing system in a state where more causal histories remain distinguishable, rather than merely disturbing it repeatedly?
reports.answer: Early state-aware control kept the causal gate open, while blindly applying the full pulse at every passage drove the comparison in the other direction.
reports.next_question: Does the open state give the same later actions more genuinely different futures, and what bodies do those futures eventually produce?

reports.title: Matched Actions Preserve Distinct Body Histories
reports.dek: An earlier controller produced more-open and more-closed versions of each organism, and the same later actions left those branches visibly different 256 steps later; the action pair chosen to maximize the early split, however, no longer separated them more than the within-organism control.
reports.question: When an early intervention changes which futures remain available, does that difference stay abstract, or does it become part of the later body?
reports.answer: The branches remained about 0.45 Hellinger units apart at step 256 under either action pair, so developmental history remained visible in form even after the specially chosen pair lost its extra leverage.
reports.next_question: Can the open branch help an organism from a new cohort reach a mature morphology named before the future is run, using actions chosen without looking at that future?

reports.title: Interventions Have More Consistent Effects After Commitment
reports.dek: As commitment arrived, later founder interventions acquired more stable spatial consequences across four different prior-action histories, so recent history had less power to rewrite the relationships among future outcomes.
reports.question: Does development merely reduce sensitivity, or does it stabilize what a later action means?
reports.answer: After the commitment turn, spatial outcome geometry became more consistent across prior histories at the population level, even though the effect was not universal in every organism.
reports.next_question: Does that stabilization follow the body's developmental age, the transplanted hidden state, or a distributed interaction between both?

reports.title: Commitment Increases Rigidity Without Convergence
reports.dek: Four plans were frozen before their outcomes: the fine-shape confirmation did not reproduce its earlier estimate, the same push lost leverage with age, sibling futures widened rather than converged, and the population of close look-alikes collapsed.
reports.question: When a developing Flow Lenia state becomes harder to redirect, are its possible forms also converging toward one narrow destination?
reports.answer: No; taken together, the four experiments show commitment as increasing rigidity and individuation, because histories become easier to tell apart while the fan of sibling outcomes keeps opening.
reports.next_question: Will the same separation between rigidity, individuation, and basin width survive in fresh genotypes and under interventions chosen by a different observer?

reports.title: Rigidity, Control, Memory, and Identity Follow Different Timelines
reports.dek: Fixed writes lose access as the body develops, feedback can still move mature morphology while it is active, released trajectories retain only part of that control, and a specimen-specific response signature is detectable across the earliest age interval tested.
reports.question: Do write access, active steerability, post-release persistence, and causal re-identifiability change together as one process?
reports.answer: They move on different schedules, so rigidity, control, memory, and identity cannot be compressed into a single developmental coordinate.
reports.next_question: Can a distributed response signature identify an unseen genotype and forecast which intervention will remain effective after release?

reports.title: Early Interventions Reveal Broad Microscopic Futures
reports.dek: An exact local rearrangement after passage eight opened increasingly different microscopic trajectories without broadly changing formation timing or adult phenotype, which remained strongly tied to organism identity.
reports.question: How much can an early, inventory-preserving rearrangement alter the future before it alters the organism-level developmental programme?
reports.answer: The microscopic paths separated strongly, while timing and coarse adult phenotype remained comparatively canalized; robustness here coexists with substantial causal freedom.
reports.next_question: Which pre-form measurement predicts whether that freedom will later contract around transition timing?

reports.title: The Same Interventions Change Effect as the Body Develops
reports.dek: Across organism-relative ages, whole-over-parts organization rose toward the morphological transition, preferred perturbations rotated away from ordinary predictability, and macroscopic identity became more canalized.
reports.question: Does the state reorganize its causal response geometry as each organism approaches its own visible transition?
reports.answer: The atlas shows a coordinated turn in information, intervention ranking, and developmental canalization, although the alignment was descriptive rather than a direct test of causation.
reports.next_question: Can the turn be found prospectively in untouched states and then challenged with fixed interventions?

reports.title: Whole-Field Organization Anticipates Formation
reports.dek: Eight exact rearrangements were fixed at each age without seeing the eventual transition, and their response landscape rotated before the organism became visibly itself.
reports.question: Can the information-response turn be detected prospectively rather than aligned after the visible event?
reports.answer: Whole-over-parts organization rose and high-score outcomes separated from ordinary predictability before formation, providing a developmental coordinate without an exact countdown.
reports.next_question: Does acting along the high-score direction before and after formation produce a consistent change in later futures?

reports.title: Formation Reorders Actions Without a Universal Sign Flip
reports.dek: The visible boundary reorganized which microscopic actions counted as high-score and low-score, but it did not rotate every organism toward one common future effect.
reports.question: Immediately around formation, does the high-score direction reliably switch from narrowing futures to widening them?
reports.answer: No universal negative-to-positive flip appeared; the action ranking changed strongly, while the later future effect remained individual and the mean turn went downward.
reports.next_question: Can an organism-specific alignment rule forecast which action will constrain its future at a given age?

reports.title: The Same Intervention Changes Effect with Age
reports.dek: The local score could be separated at every tested age, while its relationship to independent future breadth moved from constrictive before the transition to expansive around and after it.
reports.question: Does the same controllable information direction retain the same causal meaning throughout development?
reports.answer: It does not; the score remains steerable while its alignment with future narrowing changes across age, with most checkpoints fixed before their outcomes were seen.
reports.next_question: Can a fresh cohort confirm the age-dependent alignment and separate it from action re-indexing?

reports.title: Interventions Split Futures Without Shifting Formation
reports.dek: Forward and backward moves along each organism's developing information direction separated microscopic futures, while the certified body transition and coarse adult morphology barely moved on average.
reports.question: Does an information-aligned intervention act as a universal accelerator or brake on formation?
reports.answer: No; the intervention exposed different microfutures inside a canalized developmental event, with rare organisms showing more open basins.
reports.next_question: What happens when we measure the full range of responses to later interventions instead of measuring only transition time?

reports.title: Different Histories Shape Future Responses Before Visible Form
reports.dek: History-matched states already occupied different causal futures before formation, and that separation deepened through the visible event rather than appearing as a single spike.
reports.question: When do different histories first produce responses as different as those seen across the full information-score range?
reports.answer: It was already large in the earliest pre-event window examined, while morphology only gradually revealed the difference.
reports.next_question: How much earlier does that future map extend, and is it already mature at passage eight?

reports.title: Early Histories Already Shape Later Responses
reports.dek: History-dependent future displacement stayed high from roughly twenty-eight passages before formation through the crossing itself, with no evidence that the map assembled upward during those windows.
reports.question: Does the range of responses to intervention appear near the visible transition, or is it already broad much earlier?
reports.answer: The measured response range was already broad at the earliest tested stage and stayed nearly flat, while early history still strongly affected when formation occurred.
reports.next_question: Can a fixed-age assay at passage eight verify that the early map is already broad?

reports.title: Hidden-State Interventions Already Redirect the Body by Passage 24
reports.dek: At passage 24, the earliest age in this experiment, moving hidden composition along each state's own temporal direction compacted the later body, while reversing that direction expanded it.
reports.question: Does moving hidden state along its recent developmental direction change the body only when applied late, or does it work earlier too?
reports.answer: The intervention retained the same effect from passages 24 through 48, so it was already able to redirect body development at the beginning of the tested window.
reports.next_question: What changes between passages eight and 12 as that hidden-state intervention becomes stronger?

reports.title: Hidden-State Control Strengthens Between Passages 8 and 12
reports.dek: A faint preferred hidden-state direction was already measurable at passage eight. By passage 12, its effect on later body geometry had nearly doubled even though the applied dose was smaller.
reports.question: How early does a seeded field acquire a privileged direction in which an invisible composition change alters its later body?
reports.answer: Control along the preferred hidden-state direction increased sharply between passages eight and 12, before development settled into the later body, while sideways controls remained weaker.
reports.next_question: What information is being reorganized while ordinary predictability falls and directional control rises?

reports.title: Predictability Falls as Hidden-State Control Strengthens
reports.dek: Between passages eight and 12, ordinary predictive information fell while hidden composition differentiated and control along the system's own developmental direction became much stronger.
reports.question: Is organism formation simply an accumulation of predictive information, or does information change how it participates in control?
reports.answer: The measurements support a transfer from ordinary predictability toward directional causal leverage, alongside visible expansion and increasing hidden spatial variation.
reports.next_question: Can a transplant or clamp move a state across this early ignition and reproduce the later geometry change?

reports.title: Hidden-State Transplants Redirect Later Body Size
reports.dek: The hidden-state change normally seen between passages eight and 12 constrained later body radius when inserted early, while reversing that change at passage 12 released expansion.
reports.question: Is the changing hidden state merely a marker of age, or does it causally oppose the body's concurrent growth?
reports.answer: Transplanting the direction changed later body size with the sign expected from a negative-feedback constraint, even though the visible starting field was held fixed.
reports.next_question: How does the response scale with dose, and does the ordinary trajectory return after the intervention ends?

reports.title: Larger Hidden-State Pulses Stop Producing Larger Growth Changes
reports.dek: Cancelling the hidden counterweight released growth and amplifying it constrained growth, but the response saturated and later relaxed toward the ordinary trajectory.
reports.question: Does the early hidden counterweight behave like a graded actuator, and does the system preserve the induced change?
reports.answer: The body followed a nonlinear dose response with a clear native-direction advantage, then reconstructed much of its usual path after the pulse.
reports.next_question: Can repeated low-amplitude control hold the displacement long enough to alter a later transition after release?

reports.title: Brief Hidden-State Interventions Change the Body Later
reports.dek: Four half-dose pulses along one hidden direction, followed by release, changed the timing of a later body transition; the reverse and equal-energy scrambled directions did not reproduce the same effect.
reports.question: Can repeated control of an invisible early direction leave a delayed morphological consequence after the controller stops?
reports.answer: The selected native direction retained its advantage beyond the last pulse, showing a privileged developmental control axis rather than a correlation with age.
reports.next_question: Which zero-net pulse orders and amplitudes write the most persistent memory into that axis?

reports.title: Forward and Backward Hidden-State Pulses Produce Different Bodies
reports.dek: At passage 24, each state's hidden-state change between passages 24 and 40 was used to construct equal-dose forward, reverse, and sideways interventions. The forward intervention compacted the later body and, at a particular age, widened the range of subsequent futures.
reports.question: Is a state's recent temporal direction causally special, beyond the fact that any hidden rewrite can alter development?
reports.answer: Forward and reverse interventions began from identical visible fields but produced different later geometry. At one age, the forward intervention also increased the diversity of later outcomes.
reports.next_question: When does this directional effect first appear, and which parts of the hidden field carry it?

reports.title: Invisible State Rewrites Redirect Development
reports.dek: At passage 40, every visible pixel and the global channel balance were held fixed while only the hidden allocation between two material channels was rewired, and the later body changed.
reports.question: Can two states with the same visible field have different developmental futures because their hidden composition is arranged differently?
reports.answer: Yes; an exact invisible rewrite shifted later radius and trajectory, showing that visible morphology is an incomplete causal description of the state.
reports.next_question: Can each organism's own hidden direction predict which invisible rewrite will expand or compact its later body?

reports.title: An Early Intervention Narrows Later Responses on Average
reports.dek: From each organism at passage 32, eight equal pushes produced sibling states; after the higher- and lower-scoring siblings were chosen, but before any long continuation existed, both received the same unforced continuation and eight later pushes, and the higher sibling reached a slightly narrower set of passage-900 fields on average.
reports.question: Can one early push change which later responses remain accessible, even when every sibling begins from the same passage-32 state?
reports.answer: Across 30 ancestors, the higher-scoring siblings reached a narrower set of passage-900 fields on average, although twelve widened; the timing interval still included no change, and the experiment could not separate the coordinate from the action chosen to reach it.
reports.next_question: If the coordinate-guided push is repeated and then released, does the narrower response field persist, grow, or disappear?
reports.evidence_class: future-blind sibling intervention in a new cohort

reports.title: An Intervention That Works Early Stops Working Four Steps Later
reports.dek: The intervention that separated the two sibling states at passage 36 no longer produced the same difference when replayed later, even though the repeated pulses continued to change state and form.
reports.question: Can a fixed early action accumulate commitment if it is repeated at later ages?
reports.answer: It cannot reliably do so; the original information ordering closed within four steps, and later replays drove large changes along other directions.
reports.next_question: Can feedback re-evaluate the current state at every pulse and recover the future-constraining effect?

reports.title: Updating the Intervention as the State Changes Narrows Later Futures
reports.dek: A state-aware controller re-tested eight actions at every pulse, repeatedly changed its choice, rebuilt the high-versus-low information split, and recovered later future contraction without selecting on that future measurement.
reports.question: Can adaptive feedback follow the rotating information landscape better than replaying the action that worked earlier?
reports.answer: Yes; action rankings re-indexed almost completely, and adaptive selection restored both the local split and an independent contraction of microscopic futures.
reports.next_question: Does the controlled state preserve that alignment after release, or must the controller keep following it?

reports.title: Restoring the Score Does Not Restore Its Earlier Effect
reports.dek: After release erased the earlier information split, adaptive feedback found a new action and rebuilt the score difference in every organism, yet that reacquired direction no longer narrowed the independent future fan.
reports.question: If feedback can restore the local information score after release, does it also restore the earlier relation between that score and future contraction?
reports.answer: No. The score was controllable at passage 60, but the intervention no longer narrowed later futures in the same way; the action selected at passage 45 retained more of that earlier effect.
reports.next_question: Which ages align the information gradient with the future-constraining direction, and how can that alignment be forecast from the untouched state?

reports.title: States Kept Responsive Reach More Diverse Futures
reports.dek: Open, closed, untouched, and blindly forced states each received all sixty-four ordered pairs of eight later actions, allowing future diversity to be measured without categories or a chosen morphology.
reports.question: Does keeping a state responsive leave more genuinely different organisms reachable after the same later interventions?
reports.answer: The open state had roughly five more effective future dimensions than the closed state, broader raw outcome distances, and stronger sensitivity to the second action.
reports.next_question: Which visible morphologies account for the extra dimensions, and can the same later action reverse the state's preferred body?

reports.title: Earlier State Changes How Later Interventions Shape the Body
reports.dek: Open and closed developmental states received the same action pair; the action's early advantage faded, while the bodies crossed around step eighty and continued toward different late morphologies.
reports.question: Does the hidden gate state merely amplify a selected action, or does it change the direction of development after that action is no longer special?
reports.answer: The developmental mode persisted after the action-level advantage disappeared, and the open branch became larger, longer, and more skeletal under the same later causes.
reports.next_question: Can late feedback pull either gate state toward the opposite body plan and test whether the bias is negotiable?

reports.title: Later Actions Can Reverse a Body-Form Bias
reports.dek: Late feedback asked both open and closed states for either compact, solid morphology or expansive, skeletal morphology, and both states moved cleanly toward the requested target while control remained active.
reports.question: Does an early information state fix one developmental fate, or does it bias a body that later feedback can still redirect?
reports.answer: The bias was strong but negotiable; both states reached opposing body plans, and part of the change persisted after release before relaxing.
reports.next_question: Does steering morphology also move the earlier information gate, perhaps on a slower clock?

reports.title: Response-State Differences Reappear as Morphology Converges
reports.dek: Feedback targeted visible morphology without reading the information gate; the bodies separated first, then began to converge, while a difference in causal responsiveness appeared later.
reports.question: Can body-only control write a later information-state difference even when the visible morphologies no longer remain far apart?
reports.answer: In the open starting state, a clear gate-score difference appeared after 128 untouched steps and was essentially uncorrelated with the organism-level morphology split.
reports.next_question: Does that returned information state change how the next body responds to a fresh intervention?

reports.title: Morphologically Converged States Later Diverge Again
reports.dek: Two control histories reached nearly the same visible body at handoff, then separated again during untouched continuation. Their similar appearance concealed a difference in where each body would go next.
reports.question: When two developmental histories converge in appearance, have they reached the same causal state?
reports.answer: No; their later trajectories rebounded apart without another intervention, and fresh identical actions preserved rather than created that hidden split.
reports.next_question: Which dynamic coordinate can distinguish these same-looking states before their visible futures turn apart?

reports.title: Graded Spatial Repair Restores Canalization
reports.dek: The spatial arrangement present at passage eight was first scrambled and then rebuilt in twenty-five-percent steps, while genotype, material inventory, channel masses, and the outside field remained fixed.
reports.question: Does developmental organization return at one sharp threshold, or do intervention responses recover gradually as spatial relationships are restored?
reports.answer: Intervention effects became more orderly and formation timing recovered along a graded curve, with no single threshold across the tested repair doses.
reports.next_question: At what developmental age does the same exact reconstruction stop acting as a repair?

reports.title: Spatial Repair Reverses Sign Before Passage Eight
reports.dek: The inverse block map exactly reconstructed the intact passage-eight state when applied immediately. After the scrambled state developed for eight or more passages, however, the same operation reversed the response pattern and delayed formation.
reports.question: Does an exact ancestral repair retain its meaning as the current state develops away from the injury?
reports.answer: No; rescue became anti-rescue before passage eight, even though the operation preserved current inventory and was not simply a larger disturbance.
reports.next_question: Where, passage by passage, does the state stop treating the ancestral arrangement as its own?

reports.title: A Helpful Perturbation Becomes Harmful by Passage Three
reports.dek: The same inverse spatial permutation was applied at every passage from one through seven, and its effect changed from reconstructing causal possibilities to actively disrupting them around the third passage.
reports.question: How quickly does a developing state change which spatial arrangement counts as repair?
reports.answer: Most of the sign change occurred by passage three, alongside a nearby morphological turn, while equal operation size could not explain the reversal.
reports.next_question: Does the boundary follow the body's age or the hidden composition when those two are transplanted across time?

reports.title: Matched Pulses Write Opposite Causal Memories
reports.dek: Equal-sized inverse spatial pulses were applied at the same developmental instant, and their opposite directions remained legible in the next seven passages of the future action map.
reports.question: Can a brief intervention be converted into a persistent, direction-specific causal history?
reports.answer: Yes; matched physical displacement wrote opposite information-geometric memories, while the same ancestral pulse changed meaning when delayed beyond the commitment boundary.
reports.next_question: Can feedback exploit that memory to keep multiple causal histories open after the controller stops?

reports.title: Influence over Body Shape Drops After the Structural Transition
reports.dek: At nine ages, each state received one forced founder intervention and then twelve passages of release, allowing the spread among four matched founder futures to measure how redirectable the body remained.
reports.question: Where along each organism's development does the same founder-level intervention lose leverage over later morphology?
reports.answer: The intervention's influence stayed nearly constant and then fell by about fourteen percent just after the structural transition. Fixed replication splits showed the same pattern.
reports.next_question: Can an independent cohort reproduce the full age profile and show whether the intervention is losing influence or the range of possible outcomes is narrowing?

reports.title: Intervention Order Leaves Bodies in Different Later Positions
reports.dek: The same counts of high- and low-directed pulses were delivered in alternating or blocked order, after which the later future clouds moved apart while retaining nearly the same volume.
reports.question: Does temporal order become part of the causal state when total intervention counts, beginning, and ending are matched?
reports.answer: Every ancestor retained the order split after release and under identical challenge seeds, with memory appearing mainly in future position rather than breadth.
reports.next_question: What lower-dimensional coordinate records this order, and how does it interact with the information score?

reports.title: Equal Scores Can Encode Different Histories
reports.dek: Excursion and hold paths were brought back to nearly the same information-score neighborhood, then released, and their states and future clouds continued to move farther apart.
reports.question: If two histories return to the same scalar score, have they returned to the same organism?
reports.answer: They have not; the route remained encoded in body, dynamics, and future position, so the scalar compressed multiple history-dependent causal states onto one level.
reports.next_question: Can the folded geometry of those score levels be mapped directly across both history and score direction?

reports.title: Prior History Changes How the Score Responds to an Intervention
reports.dek: Across 128 matched sheets, states at nearly the same information-score level remained separated by history as strongly as states spanning much of the reachable score range, and that history changed what later actions meant.
reports.question: Is the information score a complete coordinate for the organism's causal state, or does one score level contain distinct history-dependent sheets?
reports.answer: The landscape is folded: history is a large state coordinate, the low-to-high direction depends on the sheet, and later future clouds move without a simple change in volume.
reports.next_question: Which distributed response measurements can distinguish those history-dependent states more completely?

reports.title: Intervention Order Outlasts the Final Pulse
reports.dek: Two four-pulse histories had the same zero net hidden-state dose but opposite order, and the early body followed the first pulse block rather than the last intervention.
reports.question: When total dose cancels exactly, does the order of hidden causes still direct development?
reports.answer: It does; opposite orders produced different body futures, which rules out both simple dose integration and a last-pulse explanation for the observed direction.
reports.next_question: Over which developmental ages does the body continue to understand this order as the same instruction?

reports.title: Pulse Order Changes Body Shape Early in Development, but Not Later
reports.dek: The same balanced sequence of opposing hidden-state pulses changed body geometry when applied at passages 12 through 32. At passages 48 and 64, it still changed the underlying state but no longer produced a consistent change in body radius.
reports.question: How long does the developing body retain the same response to an early hidden causal order?
reports.answer: The intervention changed body shape through passage 32, but that effect was absent at passage 48. The change therefore occurred somewhere between those two measurements; a fresh cohort also reproduced the earlier response.
reports.next_question: Does the change follow the receiving body's age or the age encoded in transplanted hidden composition?

reports.title: The Same Hidden-State Intervention Changes Effect with Age
reports.dek: At passage 32, the body expanded specifically under the hidden-state direction measured at that age. At passage 48, several directions changed connectivity instead of producing the earlier expansion.
reports.question: Does a hidden direction have a fixed meaning, or is its effect addressed to the developmental state that receives it?
reports.answer: At passage 32, the age-matched intervention specifically expanded the body. At passage 48, the response was less age-specific and affected connectivity instead, so the effect depended on the developmental state receiving the intervention.
reports.next_question: If hidden composition is swapped between passages 32 and 48, will the response follow the receiving body or the transplanted composition?

reports.title: The Recipient Body Determines Whether a Hidden-State Transplant Works
reports.dek: Aligned hidden composition was transplanted between passages 32 and 48 while the recipient's visible matter and global channel balance were preserved. Both recipients then received the same ordered pulse sequence.
reports.question: Does the response to intervention follow the age of the transplanted hidden organization or the age of the recipient body?
reports.answer: The passage-32 body remained responsive with hidden organization from passage 48, while the passage-48 body remained unresponsive with organization from passage 32. In this transplant, the response followed the recipient body.
reports.next_question: Which bodily changes between passages 36 and 44 alter the effect of the same hidden-state intervention?

reports.title: Intervention Dose Selects Distinct Body Responses
reports.dek: The same balanced passage-48 intervention was applied at different amplitudes. A half dose changed connections in the body's mid-density surface, while larger doses primarily expanded the body.
reports.question: Does increasing one intervention merely scale one response, or can the body enter different response regimes?
reports.answer: The dose curve branched, with topology peaking at half dose and radius responding most clearly at two to four times dose, despite matched direction and zero-net structure.
reports.next_question: Can one response regime prime the other when the two doses arrive in different orders?

reports.title: Mature Bodies Show Low-Density Fraying, Not Fission
reports.dek: At passage 48, an ordered pulse sequence increased the number of thresholded components, but the extra pieces were mostly tiny, mid-density peripheral structures rather than macroscopic daughters.
reports.question: Does the connectivity response at passage 48 represent genuine fission or a weaker change in the body's surface layer?
reports.answer: The signal vanished when components had to carry even a small fraction of total mass, so the experiment found density-specific fraying rather than a rise in daughter incidence.
reports.next_question: Can a surface-targeted intervention strengthen this response enough to divide the material into persistent daughters?

reports.title: Intervention Order Reaches Different Body Depths
reports.dek: A full prime-and-test dose matrix subtracted each dose alone and the untreated future, revealing that opposite dose orders left different nonlinear residues in the body's surface and dense core.
reports.question: Does the first dose change how a mature body decodes the second, even when total absolute dose is matched?
reports.answer: Yes; one order reached inward while the other remained nearer the surface, and connectivity retained a more specific memory than overall size.
reports.next_question: How does that depth-specific memory change as the unforced gap between prime and test grows?

reports.title: The Body's Response to an Earlier Intervention Reappears Later
reports.dek: The depth-specific order trace was absent at zero gap, formed after sixteen steps, changed layer and sign at later gaps, and returned strongly after 128 steps.
reports.question: Does the effect of the first intervention simply decay, or does the body pass through a sequence of different response states?
reports.answer: The trace behaved as a delayed, recurrent process rather than a fading scar, with different gaps exposing inward and surface-biased responses.
reports.next_question: Can continuous measurement locate the state transition that launches each later response without relying on a fixed elapsed time?

reports.title: Earlier Interventions Shift the Response Between Surface and Core
reports.dek: A zero-net, information-directed prime launched a delayed response that changed sign, moved between surface and dense core, and reappeared more than one hundred steps later without another intervention.
reports.question: What spatial process produces the non-monotonic memory seen across prime-to-test gaps?
reports.answer: The response behaves like a traveling reorganization between the body's surface and core. Component spacing follows the later response curve even when pixel differences remain subtle.
reports.next_question: Can the next intervention be triggered by the body's current internal organization rather than by elapsed time?

reports.title: Hidden Composition Biases Futures Without Changing Form
reports.dek: The host's visible matter field remained exactly unchanged while its pixelwise channel ratio was replaced with a donor's, and the later body moved partway toward the donor's native future.
reports.question: Can hidden composition redirect development without copying visible shape or changing total matter?
reports.answer: Yes; the donor ratio biased the trajectory while preserving the host's body and global inventory, and the recipient remained its own organism rather than becoming a donor replica.
reports.next_question: Is the useful information carried by global balance, local spatial relationships, or a combination of both?

reports.title: Where Hidden Composition Is Placed Controls Expansion and Contraction
reports.dek: Local donor composition was transplanted into the same visible body while global channel balance was held fixed, and later morphology moved toward expansive or compact donor futures with different dependence on host context.
reports.question: Does a hidden spatial arrangement act as a causal variable before visible morphology changes?
reports.answer: Both donor directions redirected development, but contraction depended more strongly on the host's overall channel balance and appeared earlier than expansion.
reports.next_question: Can we separate the effect of local spatial arrangement from the effect of overall channel composition?

reports.title: Expansion Requires Spatial Pattern; Contraction Does Not
reports.dek: Expansion depended on the intact local donor map, while contraction survived uniform and scrambled versions more readily. Hidden composition therefore controlled later form in at least two different ways.
reports.question: Does one hidden composition pattern govern both expansion and contraction?
reports.answer: The evidence points to a spatially organized expansion signal and a contraction signal carried more by overall composition. Even partial transplants changed the later body.
reports.next_question: Where do these two control modes meet across transplant fraction, host balance, and spatial scale?

reports.title: Developmental Response Depends on Multiscale Spatial Relationships
reports.dek: Rigidly moving or rotating the hidden pattern preserved much of its developmental effect, while scrambling internal spatial phase erased the direction despite matched global balance and Fourier magnitude.
reports.question: Is the hidden instruction tied to absolute coordinates, total composition, or relationships within the pattern?
reports.answer: The response depended on relationships within the pattern, tolerated changes in position and orientation, and was distributed across scales. Expansion depended more on the center, while contraction was more diffuse.
reports.next_question: How do coarse and fine spatial components contribute separately to the two developmental directions?

reports.title: Expansion Depends on Broad Pattern; Contraction Retains Fine Detail
reports.dek: Broad, spatially aligned organization carried expansion, while contraction survived isolation of fine detail and much stronger spatial scrambling. The two responses therefore depended on different features of the hidden pattern.
reports.question: Can one hidden field contain distinct instructions whose meanings depend on different spatial scales?
reports.answer: Expansion required broad spatial relationships, whereas contraction retained a usable fine-scale component and responded differently to orientation.
reports.next_question: Do unrelated organisms share any part of this syntax, or does each body supply its own private decoder?

reports.title: Equal Disruption Can Send the Body Toward Different Futures
reports.dek: Three matched paths from intact to phase-destroyed hidden patterns produced absorption, amplification, and redirection rather than one monotonic loss of developmental control.
reports.question: Does increasing phase destruction trace a single severity axis through the hidden code?
reports.answer: It does not; equal amounts of deformation can lead along different developmental routes, with expansion generally more phase-sensitive than compactification.
reports.next_question: Can those routes be mapped as directions through phase space rather than summarized by a single dose?

reports.title: Similar Bodies Can Respond in Opposite Directions
reports.dek: Changing only the spatial phase of hidden composition sent the same visible body toward futures on both sides of its native trajectory, and some sampled directions exceeded the intact donor future.
reports.question: How many developmental exits are available inside one visible present when hidden phase is varied?
reports.answer: Most starting states opened routes on both sides, while distance from the intact pattern barely predicted where a phase direction would lead.
reports.next_question: Are any phase directions readable across unrelated organisms, or is the vocabulary entirely body-specific?

reports.title: The Same Hidden Pattern Has Different Effects Across Organisms
reports.dek: Rankings across twelve phase fields were essentially uncorrelated between unrelated families, although one field repeatedly biased development toward expansion and away from compactification.
reports.question: Do different organisms respond to the same hidden spatial patterns in the same way?
reports.answer: Most response rankings were specific to each body, although one pattern produced a similar directional effect across several families.
reports.next_question: Does that pattern retain its effect when transformed or moved into families outside the original group?

reports.title: Reversing the Hidden Pattern Reverses Its Effect
reports.dek: Negating the candidate shared field reversed its developmental bias, while rotations and reflections changed the response, showing that the effect depended on sign and orientation rather than generic disorder.
reports.question: Is the candidate transferable field a directional operator or merely a perturbing texture?
reports.answer: Negating the pattern favored contraction instead of expansion, while rotations and reflections showed that the response depended on orientation. This dependence became more visible later in development.
reports.next_question: Which receiver geometry determines how this signed field is interpreted across new organisms?

reports.title: Information-Directed Dose Strengthens Identity Memory
reports.dek: Three equal-size forward and backward dose pairs tested whether an early information-directed push changed how strongly a later founder mixture remembered which founder acted first.
reports.question: Is the information-defined direction merely a sign, or does increasing its dose strengthen causal memory?
reports.answer: Identity memory rose with dose along the forward direction and weakened along the backward direction, with spatial and founder-composition memory moving together.
reports.next_question: Will the dose-dependent memory survive release and generalize to a fresh cohort with independently selected directions?

reports.title: Write Access Falls While Sibling Forms Keep Diverging
reports.dek: This synthesis joins the early response maps, selective commitment, closed-loop control, causal identity, and the four-experiment hardening study. It is retained as an earlier reading of the evidence now presented in the main synthesis.
reports.question: Across the full campaign, when does the developing field begin to constrain its future as an individual, and how does that constraint change with age?
reports.answer: The synthesis places individuality before obvious silhouette, then separates falling write access from convergence, because later states resist intervention while sibling forms continue to diverge.
reports.next_question: Can an early response signature identify an unseen genotype and predict which intervention will still work later in development?

reports.title: Flow Lenia Causal Emergence: Evidence and Open Tests
reports.dek: This early synthesis framed the project around counterfactual return after injury and asked whether whole-over-parts organization might rise before a system began correcting deviations toward a preferred endpoint.
reports.question: Could recovery toward one macroscopic state provide the first operational sign of goal-directed organization in Flow Lenia?
reports.answer: The available wound experiments did not yet establish that return, so the report served mainly as a map of tests that the later campaign made more direct.
reports.next_question: Later syntheses shift from one preferred endpoint toward the developing map of interventions, histories, and reachable futures.

reports.title: Whole-Field Organization Precedes Visible Replication
reports.dek: This early synthesis connected the prospective whole-over-parts rise with a structural information peak, proposing that higher-level organization could precede both obvious replication and settled body form.
reports.question: Does a coordinated whole change before recognizable replication-like behavior or committed morphology appears?
reports.answer: Two prospective measurements supported an early temporal signal, while the causal meaning of that signal remained unresolved and became the subject of later interventions.
reports.next_question: The next synthesis follows the question from prediction into history-dependent future structure and direct causal closure.

reports.title: Possible Futures Organize Before Coherent Form
reports.dek: This synthesis first assembled the campaign around the idea that a history-dependent action map precedes visible body form and becomes progressively harder to rewrite.
reports.question: What if organism formation begins as an organization of possibilities rather than the appearance of one recognizable shape?
reports.answer: The report connected prospective prediction, intervention ranking, future fans, and commitment, although later review found two links pointing to the wrong analyses and restored null and aborted experiments that had fallen out of view.
reports.next_question: Which parts of this account survive when every claim is checked against the experiment that produced it?

reports.title: What Remained After Checking Every Claim Against Its Experiment
reports.dek: This review corrected two misplaced evidence links, compared each planned result with the later observations, and restored the null and aborted experiments to the scientific account.
reports.question: Which claims about changing developmental responses remain supported when each one is checked against its experiment?
reports.answer: The early response map, selective commitment, history dependence, and changing effects of intervention remained supported. Several narrower claims about morphology and control remained mixed or unconfirmed.
reports.next_question: Would later control, identity, and hardening experiments support the same account of a response map becoming harder to rewrite?

reports.title: The Recovery Assay Failed to Displace Its Targets
reports.dek: This early assay tried to damage an internal state and watch whether the system returned toward a chosen visible target, but the intervention barely moved the target measurement in the first place.
reports.question: Can a pre-form system reveal a preferred future by correcting a displacement away from it?
reports.answer: The experiment did not create enough visible displacement to test recovery, so it left the goal-state question unresolved rather than demonstrating return.
reports.next_question: A stronger assay must first move a mechanically defined target, then compare active return with matched passive relaxation.

reports.title: Changing the Information Score Did Not Improve Restoration
reports.dek: For sixteen passages, feedback pushed the integrated predictive score up or down and then released the system; the score moved temporarily, while later compositional restoration remained similar across arms.
reports.question: Does direct control of the information score cause a replicator-like restoration regime after the controller stops?
reports.answer: This pilot showed state steering but not restoration control, because the score response was real and transient while the restoration comparisons stayed flat.
reports.next_question: A future test would need a stronger behavioral endpoint and a future-blind intervention chosen independently of restoration.
reports.evidence_class: discovery pilot with null behavioral endpoint

reports.title: The Information Score Did Not Predict Recovery
reports.dek: A fixed preinjury score was measured before severe damage across 288 fresh trajectories, then tested for its ability to predict later recovery in three creature families.
reports.question: Can internal coordination measured before injury forecast which runs will recover?
reports.answer: For this score, injury, and cohort, it could not; the association changed direction across families and did not improve prediction on unseen runs.
reports.next_question: The campaign therefore moved toward developmental future structure rather than treating this recovery score as a universal precursor.

reports.title: Policy Changes Composition Without Establishing Restoration
reports.dek: A score-maximizing policy produced more restoration onsets and two clean secondary trajectory differences, while both predeclared primary links between the score, action response, and fixed-horizon restoration remained uncertain.
reports.question: Does steering the information score directly predict or cause stronger compositional restoration?
reports.answer: The required primary chain did not separate, so the experiment supports changed compositional dynamics under policy but not a causal-emergence account of restoration.
reports.next_question: A new design would need to freeze the behavioral endpoint and demonstrate both score movement and later restoration on the same prospective cohort.

reports.title: Reservoir Recurrence Was Too Sparse to Test the Score
reports.dek: The census found genuine episodes in which a four-founder mixture returned after repeated passage and regrowth, but no family contained enough strict positive and negative examples for a fair precursor comparison.
reports.question: Does the reservoir ecology contain replicator-like compositional recurrence, and can an early information signal be tested against it?
reports.answer: Recurrence occurred, but the label structure was too sparse to evaluate the information score on this cohort; the score was never calculated here and therefore did not fail this test.
reports.next_question: A balanced cohort must deliberately produce within-family recurrence and non-recurrence before any precursor comparison is opened.

reports.title: Core Recurrence May Have an Early Precursor
reports.dek: Across 1,660 estimable valid episodes, a founder-composition integration score was compared with later restoration and with the timing of strict recurrence onsets.
reports.question: Does predictive integration rise before stronger restoration or recurrence-like behavior?
reports.answer: The broad relationship was flat, while all three measurable core onsets showed a narrower pre-onset rise that remained an exploratory hypothesis rather than a prospective result.
reports.next_question: The next direct test would freeze that onset rule and test it on a new cohort before any trajectories are inspected.

reports.title: Interventions Shift from Constricting to Expanding the Body
reports.dek: The sharpest early change in intervention ranking was selected from earlier response maps, and neighboring ages were then continued into full sets of futures. The interventions shifted from constricting the body at passage 24 toward expanding it later.
reports.question: Does the sharpest turn in the information compass have the same causal meaning throughout development?
reports.answer: The effect changed with age and was heterogeneous across organisms, an exploratory result that motivated later prospective alignment and sign-flip tests.
reports.next_question: The prospective studies ask whether age-specific action alignment can be fixed before any future outcomes are visible.

reports.title: Influence over Body Shape Falls After an Early Plateau
reports.dek: One founder choice sent matched states toward different morphologies before and at the structural turn, while the same leverage fell by 12.3 percent two passages later.
reports.question: Is the structural information event a narrow spike or the closing edge of a broader window in which founder identity can redirect form?
reports.answer: The reused cohort showed a plateau followed by reduced steerability, which motivated a fuller age map and disjoint-cohort confirmation rather than standing alone as the final estimate.
reports.next_question: A fresh full-age profile must test whether the drop in write access generalizes beyond this reused block.

reports.title: The Fine-Shape Commitment Signal Did Not Replicate
reports.dek: At three organism-relative ages, four intervention policies were released into eight matched futures; the frozen largest-component primary remained uncertain, while an exploratory fine-morphology comparison narrowed at the structural peak.
reports.question: Does an information-directed push reduce the diversity of future shapes, and which measurement can detect that change in advance?
reports.answer: The coarse body-allocation primary did not separate, and the finer peak-only result did not reproduce in the later fresh confirmation, so this report records the original lead rather than a settled effect.
reports.next_question: Any new shape result must begin with a fresh cohort and a single frozen morphology rule that is not chosen from the earlier peak.

reports.title: Timing Narrows While Body-Form Breadth Persists
reports.dek: A fresh classifier-selected cohort opened 1,536 long futures from passages 32, 40, and 48, while the average range of microscopic future fields stayed nearly constant across those ages.
reports.question: Does the information-compass turn coincide with a population-wide opening or collapse in the volume of reachable forms?
reports.answer: The overall spread of outcomes stayed flat on average, while transition timing and the geometry of individual futures changed. The informative differences concerned paths and alignment rather than total volume.
reports.next_question: Which path-wise or history-conditioned measurements distinguish the individual geometries hidden by a stable average volume?
reports.evidence_class: fresh-cohort replication with null volume effect

reports.title: Information-Directed Pulses Favor a Dominant Body
reports.dek: In thirty-eight reused early states, one information-forward push was released into eight new futures and reduced disagreement in how much mass consolidated into the dominant connected component.
reports.question: Can a brief information-directed intervention stabilize one feature of development without reducing the diversity of all later forms?
reports.answer: The reused cohort showed narrower dominant-body allocation under the forward push, while other morphology remained diverse; this lead was kept separate from the later fresh fine-shape confirmation, which was null.
reports.next_question: An independent cohort would need to use dominant-body allocation as its sole primary measurement before the futures are generated.

reports.title: Early Intervention Order Leaves Different Later Responses
reports.dek: A small information-selected perturbation was followed by later action sequences, testing whether the first push changed how strongly a subsequent intervention survived being overwritten.
reports.question: Can an early hidden-state intervention change how the organism responds to later interventions, rather than changing only one trajectory?
reports.answer: Resistance to a later overwrite changed, but the size and direction of that change varied across organisms. The result therefore became a more specific question about how response depends on dose.
reports.next_question: The dose-response experiment asks whether the same direction changes founder-identity memory monotonically under a new future.
